tierA_monitoring.description: Fixed source list checked on a schedule. High precision, low recall by design. A hit here means an existing pattern changed or a trusted source explicitly announced something new. All URLs below were verified live before being added.

sources.note: Already cited inline in ops/observability.md; formally registered here so schedule checks catch updates. Also covers session-level metrics needed for session-economics node.

sources.title: AgentCore — VPC configuration
sources.note: Already cited inline in external/providers.md; formally registered here.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
sources.note: Primary backing source for the code-intelligence node. Covers chunking, embedding, retrieval, and namespace isolation for RAG over indexed data sources. Verify URL on first use — AWS docs restructure occasionally.

sources.note: Verified live 2026-08-14. Hub page for enterprise deployment. Covers: API provider selection (Anthropic, Bedrock, GCP, Azure), managed settings delivery, policy enforcement (permission rules, sandboxing, MCP control, plugin marketplaces, model restrictions), usage visibility, and data handling. SSO and SCIM provisioning reference the Claude Enterprise Administrator Guide separately.

sources.title: Claude Code — Server-managed settings
sources.note: Centralized policy delivery from the claude.ai admin console. Backs the 'org-wide policy overrides individual developer settings' principle in harness-selection and guardrails.

sources.title: Claude Code — Managed MCP servers
sources.note: Covers org-level MCP server allowlists, denylists, and managed-only enforcement — directly backs the MCP server approval model in registry/mcpservers and the catalog governance decision.

sources.title: Claude Code — Claude Apps Gateway spend limits
sources.note: Verified indirectly via admin-setup 2026-08-14. Covers per-user and per-group spend limits through the Claude Apps Gateway — directly backs the alert/throttle/block enforcement model and policy-tier exceptions.

sources.title: Claude Code — Monitoring usage
sources.note: OpenTelemetry export of sessions, tools, and tokens. All providers. Backs the OTel-compatible telemetry decision in ops/observability.

sources.title: Claude Code — Analytics
sources.note: Adoption and contribution metrics dashboard (Teams/Enterprise) and per-user usage/spend (Console). Backs cost attribution and adoption analytics.

sources.title: Claude Code — Zero Data Retention
sources.note: ZDR option for qualified Claude Enterprise accounts. Nothing stored after request completes. Backs the data-handling decision in security-posture and the model-provider compliance posture.

sources.title: Claude Code — Legal and compliance
sources.note: Regulatory certifications and compliance framework coverage. Backs the compliance-posture decisions in security-posture.

sources.title: Claude Code — LLM gateway
sources.note: Single endpoint in front of multiple providers with centralized request logging. Backs model gateway decisions and the SaaS product's built-in gateway capability.

sources.title: Claude Code — Self-hosted environments
sources.note: Self-hosted deployment option for Claude Code. Relevant to the SaaS-product harness selection for air-gapped or strict-residency environments.

sources.title: PydanticAI — Documentation
sources.note: Canonical URL — ai.pydantic.dev redirects here. Covers agent loop, typed tools, dependency injection, multi-model support, MCP, and the Coder harness (clai CLI). Changelog at pydantic.dev/docs/ai/project/changelog/

sources.title: Microsoft AutoGen — Documentation
sources.note: AutoGen 0.4 (agentchat + core + ext). Covers DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor, team patterns (SelectorGroupChat, Swarm, GraphFlow), MCP via autogen-ext. Releases at github.com/microsoft/autogen/releases

sources.title: CrewAI — Documentation
sources.note: Covers Crews (sequential/hierarchical), Flows (event-driven), MCP via MCPServerAdapter. Note: changelog URL is version-pinned in Mintlify — monitor docs.crewai.com root for current path.

sources.title: Hugging Face smolagents — Documentation
sources.note: Key claim to verify on each check: CodeAgent ~30% fewer steps vs tool-calling. Sandbox options (E2B, Blaxel, Modal, Docker). LocalPythonExecutor is explicitly NOT a security boundary — verify this warning persists in docs.

sources.title: Google ADK — Documentation
sources.note: Canonical URL — google.github.io/adk-docs/ redirects here. Multi-language SDKs across separate repos: adk-python, adk-js, adk-go, adk-java, adk-kotlin. Release notes at adk.dev/release-notes/

sources.title: Agno — Documentation
sources.note: Formerly PhiData. AgentOS runtime — 50+ REST endpoints, JWT RBAC, BYOC. MCPTools class. Monitor for changes to multi-tenant isolation model.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents SDK — Documentation
sources.note: Distinct from openai/codex (the CLI harness). Framework SDK: Agent + Handoff + Guardrail + Session + SandboxAgent. Release notes at openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/release/

sources.title: AG2 — Documentation
sources.note: Community AutoGen fork — distinct from Microsoft AutoGen 0.4. Protocol-driven rewrite with Network + Hub + typed Channels architecture. v1.0 stabilized Aug 2026.

sources.title: Strands Agents — User guide
sources.note: Added 2026-08-14. Architecture overview and agent lifecycle for the Strands OSS framework. Backs harness-selection/oss-frameworks. Domain known-good (other Strands pages already in Tier A); specific path to verify on first citation use.

sources.title: Strands Agents — Multi-agent patterns
sources.note: Added 2026-08-14. Agent-to-agent delegation and fan-out. Corroborates registry/subagents depth/fan-out caps and backs oss-frameworks assembly model. Path to verify on first citation use.

sources.title: MCP — Security best practices
sources.note: Verified live 2026-08-14. Versioned URL (spec version 2026-07-28) — update path when MCP spec advances. Covers: confused deputy attacks, token passthrough, SSRF, local MCP server compromise (supply chain), OAuth URL validation (XSS/RCE), stdio transport security, scope minimization. Directly backs security-posture node and strengthens provenance's supply-chain risk framing.

sources.note: Verified live 2026-08-13 (developers.openai.com/codex redirects here). Candidate for Tier C corroboration on exec/perms/loop — cite once a specific claim is verified against content.

sources.title: LangChain — Agents
sources.note: Verified live 2026-08-14 (python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/agents redirects to docs.langchain.com). Explicitly states 'Agent = Model + Harness' and 'an agent is a model calling tools in a loop until a task is complete.' Corroborates the reason-act-observe loop shape independently of Anthropic/AWS sources. Also covers tool use, middleware, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop patterns.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
sources.note: Verified live 2026-08-14. Current version: 2026 (published 2026-08-04). Key categories for this knowledge base: LLM01 (Prompt Injection), LLM05 (Supply Chain Vulnerabilities), LLM07 (Insecure Plugin Design → MCP server risk), LLM08 (Excessive Agency → autonomy mode / guardrails). Note: active development has moved to the OWASP GenAI Security Project — monitor both this page and https://genai.owasp.org for updates.

sources.title: Anthropic — Model pricing
sources.note: Concrete per-token costs by model tier (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus classes). Required for model-tiering node's cost-per-tier reasoning and session-economics cost estimates. Prices change — this MUST be checked on schedule, not just at authoring time. Never assert a specific price figure in a component file without noting 'as of <date>'.

sources.title: HashiCorp Vault — AWS IAM auth method
sources.note: IAM auth configuration; binding Lambda roles to Vault policies; cross-account trust. Core auth method for the vault-credential-broker pattern.

sources.title: HashiCorp Vault — Agent
sources.note: Sidecar pattern; auto-auth; template rendering; lease renewal. Backs the ECS sidecar deployment option in vault-integration.

sources.title: HashiCorp Vault — KV v2 secrets engine
sources.note: Versioned KV; metadata; read/write API. Primary static secrets pattern in the gateway credential broker.

sources.title: HashiCorp Vault — AWS secrets engine
sources.note: Dynamic AWS credentials; STS AssumeRole; lease TTL. Backs the dynamic-secrets recommendation in vault-integration.

sources.title: Jupyter Server REST API
sources.note: Kernel management, content API, session API. Foundation for the Jupyter MCP server tool definitions.

sources.title: jupyter_client — kernel protocol
sources.note: ZeroMQ messaging; execute_request; output capture. Required for cell execution capability in the Jupyter MCP server.

sources.title: Zero to JupyterHub on Kubernetes
sources.note: JupyterHub on EKS; single-user pod configuration; singleuser.extraContainers for MCP server sidecar. Primary deployment reference for the JupyterLab surface.

sources.title: Federal Reserve SR 11-7 — Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management
sources.checkMethod: manual — stable supervisory letter; check annually for updates or successor guidance
sources.note: 2011 guidance; foundation for MRM programs at Fed-supervised institutions. Stable document — annual check sufficient. Do not interpret for AI application without compliance counsel.

sources.title: OCC Bulletin 2021-38 — Model Risk Management Principles for Banks Using AI
sources.checkMethod: manual — stable bulletin; check annually for successor guidance
sources.note: Most directly applicable OCC guidance for AI systems. Published 2021. Explicitly addresses AI model risk. Check annually for successor guidance as AI regulation evolves.

sources.title: FINRA Rule 4511 — Books and Records
sources.checkMethod: manual — stable rule text; check annually for amendments
sources.note: Record-keeping requirements for broker-dealers. Application to AI session logs requires counsel interpretation. Stable rule text — annual check.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Cloud Run documentation
sources.note: Service configuration, VPC connector, minimum instances, Workload Identity. Primary reference for Cloud Run deployment option in gcp-runner.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Workload Identity Federation
sources.note: Pool and provider configuration; AWS provider setup; token exchange. Core authentication pattern for GCP runner — no static credentials.

sources.title: Google Cloud — Cloud Logging structured logging (Python)

sources.title: CyberArk — Central Credential Provider REST API

sources.title: CyberArk Conjur — documentation
sources.note: JWT authentication; secret retrieval API; OIDC integration. Alternative to legacy CCP for organizations on Conjur cloud-native platform.

sources.note: PCAOB standard governing external auditor assessment of ITGC. Stable — annual check. Backs ITGC evidence requirements in sox node.

sources.note: Canonical docs for Pi harness. URL provided 2026-08-16. GitHub repo confirmed: earendil-works/pi (~91k stars). Docs explicitly state: four default tools (read, write, edit, bash), no built-in sandbox, operator must provide container/VM/microVM isolation.

sources.note: Root redirects to /cline-overview. Primary source for MCP integration model, approval flows, and IDE extension capabilities.

sources.title: OpenHands — Documentation
sources.note: Canonical docs domain is docs.openhands.dev — project rebranded from All Hands AI. Repo is OpenHands/OpenHands (~84k stars). Covers browser client (Agent Canvas), CLI, REST/WebSocket APIs. Wraps Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and ACP-compatible agents as substrates. No desktop app — deprecated local GUI only.

sources.note: TypeScript-native AI agent framework. Repo is mastra-ai/mastra (~27k stars). License: Apache 2.0 core + proprietary EE (ee/ directories). Studio UI confirmed at localhost:4111. MCP server authoring supported. 'Harness primitive launched June 2026' claim unconfirmed from canonical docs — monitor for official announcement.

sources.note: Root swe-agent.com redirects to /latest/. Purpose-built GitHub issue → code fix pipeline. Main repo is in MAINTENANCE MODE as of 2026-08-16 — active development shifted to mini-swe-agent. Monitor mini-swe-agent repo for feature parity and adoption.

sources.note: Main repo in maintenance mode as of 2026-08-16. Monitor for official deprecation or redirect notice.

sources.title: SWE-bench — Leaderboard
sources.note: The authoritative benchmark for coding agent harness quality on real GitHub issues. Maintained by Princeton NLP / SWE-agent team. Covers all agents, not just SWE-agent. Weekly check warranted — leaderboard updates frequently as new agents are evaluated.

tierB_discovery.description: Broader, noisier sweep. Purpose is to find named patterns NOT already represented in the taxonomy. A finding only becomes a candidate if it clears corroborationThreshold below.
tierB_discovery.trigger: on-demand only — run via `node scripts/manage-discovery.mjs run` or an equivalent discovery-sweep skill. Never scheduled/cron'd; the user initiates every run manually.

corroborationThreshold.rule: A candidate component/pattern must appear, consistently named, across at least this many sources that do not cite each other. Tripwire-only sources never count toward this threshold.

deferredComponents.description: Components identified during gap audits as medium-confidence — real but less settled. Each discovery-sweep run should check whether these have cleared the corroboration threshold.

candidates.name: Data residency / VPC placement as its own axis
Progressive trust elevation — teams earn relaxed guardrails over time
Org-wide and team-wide standards injection (CLAUDE.md, ADRs) as platform component

tierB_discovery.tripwireNote: Aggregator hits are a signal to look closer, never evidence on their own. Do not count a tripwire hit toward the >=2-source corroboration requirement.

tierC_caseStudies.description: Real org/vendor precedent for a specific ## Decisions option, backfilling components that currently assert a pattern with no citable source. Every Tier C source entry must state 'as of <date>' in its supports text when used in a component file — never presented as current fact, only historical precedent.
